display.purpose: Page titles only. One per page. Never inside cards.

headline.purpose: AI insight headlines. Dense informational heading where the data headline is the message.

title.purpose: Card section titles, panel headers. One level below Display; used inside cards.

body.purpose: Primary UI text — table cells, form values, insight copy. Cap prose at 65–75ch.

label.purpose: Secondary UI — form labels, table column headers, meta information.

mono.purpose: Tabular numeric data — accuracy percentages, question counts, session numbers.

shadows.name: brand-glow
shadows.purpose: Sidebar brand logo mark only. One deliberate use; its singularity makes the brand mark feel anchored.

shadows.name: surface-lift
shadows.purpose: Floating elements above the page surface — future dropdowns, popovers, command palettes. Not yet used; defined to establish vocabulary.

shadows.name: modal-lift
shadows.purpose: Full modal dialogs and overlay sheets. Must clearly separate from all page content.

motion.name: ease-standard
motion.purpose: Default transition for all UI state changes — hover, active, focus. Fast enough to feel responsive, slow enough to feel deliberate.

motion.name: row-highlight
motion.purpose: New-row flash animation in Study Sessions table. Background-color from accent tint to transparent.

breakpoints.name: mobile-cap
breakpoints.note: Sidebar collapses below this threshold. Not yet implemented — see audit P1 responsive gap.

narrative.overview:
The interface surfaces data the way a case file surfaces facts — methodically, without decoration. Every metric on screen exists to answer one question: what should I study next? If a data point does not serve that judgment, it does not earn space. The AI coach is the analyst; the user is the credentialed expert who decides.

This is a tool, not an experience. The reference is Linear: dense, keyboard-first, deliberately unglamorous. The system is quiet so the data can be loud.

What this system explicitly rejects: the generic SaaS AI aesthetic (purple gradients, hero metrics, "Sign up for free" energy); clinical hospital software (grey-on-grey EMR aesthetics); and gamified study apps (streak counters, reward animations, encouragement theater).
keyCharacteristics: System-font stack — no loaded display fonts; renders natively on all platforms
Signal Blue (#0A84FF) appears on interactive and data-state elements only — never decorative
Flat surface hierarchy — borders and background tints separate layers; shadows for floating elements only
Dense but breathable — table rows are tight; card padding is generous; the contrast is intentional
Semantic state vocabulary — success/danger/warning have fixed hex values with verified contrast ratios

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Signal Blue appears on ≤10% of any given screen. The moment it decorates something non-interactive, it loses its meaning as a direction signal.

rules.name: The Semantic Fence Rule
rules.body: Success, Danger, and Warning colors are reserved exclusively for performance states and validation. Prohibited as general-purpose accents or branding elements.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Tertiary Ink (#8A8A8F) is prohibited on text smaller than 18px (or smaller than 14px bold). Every new element using tertiary ink must pass the 3.20:1 large-text threshold before shipping.

rules.name: The No-Personality Rule
rules.body: No display fonts. No custom type. Warmth comes from copy and data specificity, not from a humanist serif or custom script.

rules.name: The Tabular Fence Rule
rules.body: All numeric data must use tabular-nums and the monospace stack. Mixed proportional and tabular numbers in the same column is prohibited.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Content surfaces are never elevated. Shadows appear only on elements that genuinely float above the layout — dropdowns, modals, command palettes.

rules.name: The One Glow Rule
rules.body: The Brand Glow shadow (rgba(10,132,255,0.45)) is singular — the sidebar brand logo mark only. No other element uses a colored shadow.

dos: Do use Signal Blue (#0A84FF) only on interactive elements and active states.
Do use text-secondary (#6B6B70) as the default for all informational text that isn't primary content.
Do use placeholder:text-secondary on all form inputs — tertiary ink fails WCAG AA at placeholder sizes.

Do replace alert() validation with inline

adjacent to the failing field.
Do wire aria-current="page" on active nav links.
Do wrap async AI output panels in aria-live="polite" aria-atomic="true".
Do annotate every <label> with htmlFor matching its input's id.
Do apply tabular-nums and the mono stack to all numeric data.
Do use rounded-sm (8px) for interactive elements and rounded-md (12px) for containers.
Do keep the prefers-reduced-motion override in index.css.
donts: Don't use purple gradients, violet tints, cyan-on-dark, or multi-hue gradients as accents.
Don't use border-left or border-right > 1px as a colored stripe on cards or alerts.
Don't use background-clip: text with a gradient. Gradient text is never meaningful.
Don't use alert() for validation — use inline role="alert" instead.
Don't use Tertiary Ink (#8A8A8F) on text ≤14px weight 400–500.
Don't remove the prefers-reduced-motion override from index.css.
Don't design for generic SaaS AI aesthetic — no hero metrics with gradient accents, no AI badges.
Don't design for clinical/hospital software aesthetics — no grey-on-grey, no heavy borders.
Don't gamify — no streaks, no reward animations, no encouragement theater.
Don't nest cards inside cards. Gray-50 panel inside a white card is the only permitted interior tint.
Don't use resize on textareas — resize-none is required.
